B. Is this measure already running in Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county (or in the Tays university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Standardised lung cancer pathway with booked slots. A lung cancer pathway on the Danish/Swedish/Norwegian model: fixed referral criteria, pre-booked CT, PET-CT, bronchoscopy and MDT slots, a named pathway owner, and published time limits for each step.
supported_en: A single-region Italian study (Life 2025) found a fast-track pathway with pre-booked slots cut the average time to diagnosis by about 18 days (42.9 to 25.0).
not_supported_en: None of the pages I read measures days saved from first symptom to treatment in a Nordic or Finnish setting.
in_use_quote: Tutkimukset aloitetaan yleensä keuhkojen ja ylävatsan tietokonekerroskuvauksella, joka suoritetaan useimmiten viikon sisällä lähetteen käsittelystä.
missing_en: No page shows published time limits for each step, pre-booked PET-CT, bronchoscopy or specialist team meeting slots, a named pathway owner, or monitoring against time limits.
summary_en: I found part of this measure already in place at Tays. Pirha's patient pathway for Tays lung cancer care says that urgent referrals are usually handled within 1–2 working days. A nurse books the tests, CT is usually done within a week, and the results appointment is booked before the CT. On the effect, an Italian fast-track study (Life 2025) used pre-booked test slots, a case manager and weekly specialist team meetings. It cut the average time to diagnosis from 42.9 to 25.0 days, about 18 days. That is time to diagnosis, not from first symptom to treatment.
unanswered_en: I found no Nordic study of days saved from first symptom to treatment, and I did not check whether the Filha national guideline sets time limits for each step.
